The review covers recent advances in flexible EMI shielding materials, focusing on design strategies and multifunctionality.
Flexible EMI shielding materials are essential for wearable and portable electronics due to their lightweight and multifunctional properties.
The green shielding index (g_s) is a metric that quantifies the balance between shielding effectiveness and absorption versus reflection.
Efficient EMI shielding materials typically have a shielding effectiveness (SE) of ≥ 30 dB.
A green shielding index (g_s) of 1 or higher indicates high shielding effectiveness and good impedance matching.
The total shielding effectiveness (SE_T) is the sum of reflection loss (SE_R), absorption loss (SE_A), and multiple reflection loss (SE_M).
Reflection loss (SE_R) increases with the conductivity of the shielding material.
Multiple reflection loss (SE_M) can enhance shielding effectiveness by increasing the path length of electromagnetic waves within the material.
Graphene aerogel is a promising intrinsically flexible EMI shielding material due to its lightweight, high conductivity, and porous 3D structure.
MXene-based materials offer high electrical conductivity and unique physicochemical properties, making them suitable for flexible EMI shielding.
Impedance matching is crucial for promoting absorption and reducing secondary reflections in EMI shielding materials.
Multifunctional properties of flexible EMI shielding materials include thermal conductivity, hydrophobicity, transparency, and sensing capabilities.
The 'brick-slurry' structure in RGO-based films facilitates the construction of conductive paths, leading to high EMI performance.
Challenges in developing flexible EMI shielding materials include achieving high shielding effectiveness, maintaining flexibility, ensuring mechanical stability, and minimizing secondary reflections.
The review discusses the importance of hierarchical structures (like porous, hollow-like) in EMI shielding materials.
The green shielding index (g_s) is defined by the formula: g_s = S11^2 - S21^2 - 1, where S11 and S21 are the input reflection and transmission coefficients, respectively.
The review highlights the need for materials that minimize harmful secondary reflections while maximizing absorption.
Flexible EMI shielding materials can be categorized into intrinsically flexible materials and flexible composite materials.
Intrinsically flexible materials include graphene aerogel, carbon nanotube sponge, MXene foam, and fibrous polymer.
Flexible composite materials include nanoscale carbon composite flexible materials, flexible MXene-based composite materials, and polymer-based flexible composite materials.
The review emphasizes the importance of mechanical stability and environmental adaptability in flexible EMI shielding materials.
The review discusses the role of vector network analyzers in testing the EMI shielding ability of materials.
The review highlights the significance of the 'green EMI shielding' concept in reducing environmental harm.
The review provides insights into the future design strategies and research directions for advanced flexible EMI shielding materials.
